item.title: Birds & Bikes — Sat Oct 3, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop

item.title: Nacho and the Dollar Menu Live — Sat Oct 3, 8:00 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description:
Nacho and the Dollar Menu was originally formed by Thomas Ignacio Molina in 2014. The mission of Nacho and The Dollar Menu is to help keep Northern Californian Latino music alive and well. The band plays a mix of original music, classic covers and new music reimagined through the lens of Latino musical styles. Heavily influenced by the bands from the Mission in San Francisco and especially fond of cumbia and Chicano oldies, the band functions as a creative outlet for its members and a cultural preservation organization. Whether you’re in dancing shoes or you just want to enjoy some classic NorCal vibes, Nacho and the Dollar Menu has something for you. Instagram Little Sunflower (Video Clip) Didn’t Cha Know (Video Clip) $20 General Admission This is BYOB event 7:30 Doors 8:00 Show
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Craft and Vintage Fair — Sun Oct 4, 10:00 AM — Central Park – Davis
item.description:
Davis Craft and Vintage Fair began as the Square Tomatoes Craft Fair more than 10 years ago! The event was started by instructors from the UC Davis Craft Center in order to have a monthly craft fair for local artisans and the local community. We embraced local vintage vendors in 2017, we’ve grown and we are still home to local artists and makers from the Davis and greater Sacramento area. We collaborate with local non-profits starting with Couleurs Vives Art Studio who joined us in 2018! Many of our talented vendors can be found at other festivals like the Davis Phoenix Coalition’s Pride Fest, the I-House’s International Festival, and 2nd Friday ArtAbouts on E Street Plaza. Expect to see friendly vendors with local handmade and original art, crafts, quality vintage items, upcycled treasures, earth-friendly creations, good food, and more. Free live music fills the open space for a lively atmosphere so be sure to stop by and join us!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Rotary Club of Davis Centennial Celebration — Sun Oct 4, 5:00 PM — Veterans Memorial Theatre
item.description: Rotary Club of Davis to celebrate 100 years of service The Rotary Club of Davis will mark its centennial with a community celebration from 5 to 8 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 4, at the Davis Veterans Memorial Center. Founded in 1926 under the auspices of Rotary International, the Rotary Club of Davis has spent a century combining service, fellowship and civic involvement. The original Davis club is now one of three Rotary clubs in the city, along with Sunrise Rotary Club of Davis and Sunset Rotary Club of Davis. Tickets for the centennial dinner are $45 and include dinner by Simply Satisfied Catering. For tickets, contact Donna Prebys at 630-803-7954. Dave Scheiber will serve as master of ceremonies. The evening’s program will include a presentation on a century of Davis Rotary by Michael Peterson and Jonathan Bayless, a Rotary trivia contest led by Bruce and Marjorie Hartsough, and remarks about the club’s future from Prebys, the club’s 2026-27 president. item.title: Mercy Hawkins: Waltz of Life & Limb — Sat Oct 3 — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Mercy Hawkins: Waltz of Life & Limb Exhibit: October 3 – November 6, 2026 Reception: October 9, 6-9 PM (Free) Waltz of Life & Limb pairs recent sculptural paintings by artist Mercy Hawkins, with her vibrant, large-scale watercolors on paper. With this work, Hawkins seeks to answer the internal call, to encounter what the body already knows, from our own inner rhythms, heartbeat, and breath, to dancing with wild arms. Her biomorphic shapes, formed of intersecting dots, dashes, and lines, speak to a sensory play of color, light, and movement. Her imagery evokes seed pods, flower buds, or microscopic creatures, immersing the viewer in an all-encompassing perception of nature. Artist Talk: Saturday, October 17, 2-3:30 PM (Free) Mercy Hawkins will speak about the development and trajectory of several bodies of recent work, including its connection to craft. She will also explore the intersection of painting and music. Sponsored by HF Richardson Image: Mercy Hawkins, “Melting Ice”

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Oct 3, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Sat Oct 3, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

item.title: Author talk by Peter Flax: Why We Ride — Thu Oct 22, 5:30 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
Join us for an inspiring and enlightening look at the reasons that make people fall in love with bicycle riding! Author Peter Flax will share his insights into the creation and production of Live to Ride: Finding Joy and Meaning on a Bicycle, his 2024 book which explores the unifying dynamics of bicycle culture.
The book argues that everyone who rides—whether they commute, enjoy nature, or race—has more in common than they might realize. Part of the discussion will focus on a section contextualizing the significance of groundbreaking bike lanes constructed decades ago in Davis—and how Flax was aided by photography and documents from our Archives and Special Collections Department.
This talk is free and open to all. Please register in advance to reserve your spot.

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Dec 9, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.title: Banned Books Week — Sun Oct 4
item.description:
Banned Books Week was launched in 1982 in response to a sudden surge in the number of challenges to books in libraries, bookstores, and schools. Held in the last week of September or first week of October, the annual event highlights the value of free and open access to information and brings together the entire book community — librarians, educators, authors, publishers, booksellers, and readers of all types — in shared support of the freedom to seek and to express ideas. The next Banned Books Week will be held October 4–10, 2026. The theme of this year’s event is: Let Books Be — Protect the Freedom to Read.
Source: Hate-Free Together
